title: Knowledge check: Route Organization and Not-Found Routing

questions.prompt: In Route Organization and Not-Found Routing, which statement best describes Specific and general route ordering?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.
This option describes a different concept and does not define specific and general route ordering (choice 2).
questions.answer_key: Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.
questions.explanation: Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Route Organization and Not-Found Routing?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Routing is a contract between a method, path, parameters, and handler chain. Validate request-derived values and register specific routes before general fallbacks; Express 5 path syntax differs from Express 4.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Routing is a contract between a method, path, parameters, and handler chain. Validate request-derived values and register specific routes before general fallbacks; Express 5 path syntax differs from Express 4.
questions.explanation: Routing is a contract between a method, path, parameters, and handler chain. Validate request-derived values and register specific routes before general fallbacks; Express 5 path syntax differs from Express 4.

questions.prompt: A change related to Route Organization and Not-Found Routing appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
